symptoms_or_prerequisites: Symptoms typically develop after an incubation period of 4–7 days (range 3–14 days)
recommended_action: Consider the possible clinical presentations: asymptomatic infection, undifferentiated fever, dengue fever, dengue haemorrhagic fever, or expanded dengue syndrome.
exclusions_or_missing_information: These classifications do not establish a diagnosis in an individual patient.
evidence_passage: Symptomatic patients may have one of the following conditions: Undifferentiated fever, DF, DHF, Expanded dengue syndrome (rare).

recommended_action: Consider classical dengue fever as a possible diagnosis when the characteristic clinical presentation is present.
exclusions_or_missing_information: Clinical features alone do not confirm dengue infection.
evidence_passage: A proportion of patients infected with dengue virus develop classical dengue fever characterized by high fever, severe headache, retro-orbital pain, myalgia, arthralgia and rashes.

symptoms_or_prerequisites: Fever typically lasts 2–7 days in the majority of cases
recommended_action: Record fever onset, measured temperature, duration and pattern when assessing possible dengue.
exclusions_or_missing_information: Fever pattern alone is insufficient to diagnose dengue.
evidence_passage: The body temperature is usually between 39 °C and 40 °C (102° F to 104° F). The fever may be biphasic, lasting 2–7 days in the majority of cases.

symptoms_or_prerequisites: Rash during acute fever or around defervescence
recommended_action: Assess rash appearance and timing, including early flushing or blanching erythema, later maculopapular rash, and possible confluent erythema with spared normal skin around defervescence.
exclusions_or_missing_information: Rash alone does not confirm dengue.
Rash may not be present in every patient.
evidence_passage: Convalescent rash is characterized by confluent erythematous eruption with sparing areas of normal skin. It is often pruritic.

recommended_action: Check for intense continuous abdominal pain or abdominal tenderness; persistent vomiting (at least 3 episodes in 1 hour or at least 4 in 6 hours); fluid accumulation; mucosal bleeding; altered mental status; hepatomegaly at least 2 cm below the costal margin; and progressive haematocrit increase in two consecutive measurements 6 hours apart.
exclusions_or_missing_information: Ask about vomiting frequency and timing.
Assess abdominal pain, bleeding and mental status.
Check for fluid accumulation and hepatomegaly.
Two haematocrit measurements are needed to evaluate the stated trend.
evidence_passage: Warning signs of dengue fever (CDC 2024): intense continuous abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, fluid accumulation, mucosal bleeding, altered mental status, hepatomegaly, and progressive increase of the haematocrit.
